steps.name: QC and DESeqDataSet setup for 2x4x3 design
caveats: Confirm time is treated as a factor (t0..t3), not numeric, since only 4 levels are present and a categorical treatment of time is what the interaction LRT below requires
Do not drop replicates for being visually distinct on PCA without a documented reason
steps.context: Input is /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-without-timecourse-2x4-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 25 columns: gene symbol + 24 samples) and /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-without-timecourse-2x4-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (24 rows x 4 columns: sample, condition, time, time_hours). Design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0..t3) x 3 replicates, raw integer counts from salmon.
steps.question: Do the 24 samples in counts.csv and metadata.csv cluster as expected by condition and time (t0..t3), and what is the appropriate DESeq2 design after filtering low-count genes?
acceptance_criteria: DESeqDataSet is built with condition and time as factors matching metadata exactly (24 samples retained unless a specific sample is flagged as an outlier with justification)
Genes with near-zero counts across all samples are filtered before dispersion estimation; the number of genes retained out of 12000 is reported
A PCA plot and a sample-distance heatmap (vst-transformed) are produced and show whether samples separate by condition and/or time
Size factors and dispersion estimates are reported; any sample flagged as an outlier is explicitly justified, not silently dropped

steps.name: DESeq2 LRT for condition:time interaction
caveats: With only 3 replicates per condition-time cell, power for the interaction term is limited; report this explicitly rather than treating padj<0.05 as a strong filter on effect size
Do not confuse the reduced-model time term (shared trend) with the interaction term when reporting results — they answer different questions
steps.context: Uses the filtered DESeqDataSet and confirmed condition/time factors from T1S1. The full model ~condition + time + condition:time is compared by likelihood-ratio test against the reduced model ~condition + time; the reduced model already absorbs any time effect common to both conditions, so genes significant in this LRT are specifically treatment-by-time dependent.
steps.question: Which genes have a condition:time interaction effect — i.e. show a treatment-specific trajectory across t0..t3 beyond the time trend shared by both conditions?
acceptance_criteria: LRT is run with full = ~condition + time + condition:time and reduced = ~condition + time, using the filtered counts and confirmed factor design from T1S1
Interaction terms use a wide (unshrunk) LFC prior as is standard for DESeq2 interaction designs; main-effect LFCs are not used to call interaction significance
BH-adjusted p-values (padj) are reported per gene; a threshold (padj < 0.05) is applied and the number of interaction-significant genes out of the filtered gene set is stated

Per-timepoint condition effect (condition vs its reference, within each of t0..t3) is also extracted via contrasts on an expanded condition:time grouping, to characterize when in the time course the divergence appears
Output is a ranked gene table (gene symbol, LRT stat, padj, per-timepoint condition log2FC) suitable for input to clustering and enrichment

steps.name: Trajectory clustering of interaction genes
caveats: Cluster count should be chosen from the data (e.g. gap statistic or a small explicit sweep), not fixed arbitrarily without justification
If fewer than ~20 genes pass the interaction threshold, report patterns qualitatively rather than forcing a multi-cluster partition on a small set
steps.context: Takes the interaction-significant gene list and per-timepoint condition log2FC / vst-normalized expression from T2S1. Groups genes by the shape of their condition-specific trajectory across t0..t3 rather than reporting only a flat significant/not-significant call.
steps.question: Among genes with a significant condition:time interaction, what distinct temporal divergence patterns exist (e.g. early- vs late-onset, transient vs sustained, up- vs down-diverging in the treated condition relative to control)?
acceptance_criteria: vst-normalized expression for interaction-significant genes is averaged per condition x timepoint to build per-gene trajectory vectors
Genes are clustered on these trajectories (e.g. hierarchical or fuzzy clustering) into a small number of interpretable pattern groups
A heatmap of interaction-significant genes ordered by cluster, and representative trajectory line plots (mean +/- replicate spread per condition across t0..t3) per cluster are produced
Each cluster is labeled with its qualitative pattern (e.g. early-diverging, late-diverging, transient, monotonic) based on the per-timepoint condition effect sign and magnitude

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-specific temporal genes
caveats: WikiPathways and GO-BP gene sets are HGNC symbols matching this human dataset's gene symbols directly — no ID mapping step should be needed, but confirm symbol overlap before running ORA
GO-BP is a nested hierarchy; expect correlated parent/child terms among hits and collapse or note this rather than reporting a raw term count as independent findings
steps.context: Human (taxon 9606) gene sets are needed: WikiPathways human pathways and/or MSigDB Hallmark / GO-BP human gene sets are staged as GMT files. The interaction-significant gene list (and cluster labels) from T2S1/T3S1 are the input; the background/universe for over-representation is all genes retained after filtering in T1S1, not the full unfiltered 12000.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are over-represented among genes with a condition:time interaction, and do the pattern-clusters from T3S1 map to distinct pathways?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis (ORA) is run on the interaction-significant gene set (padj<0.05 from T2S1) against WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark/GO-BP human gene sets, using the T1S1 filtered gene set as background
If T3S1 produced multiple interpretable pattern clusters, ORA is additionally run per cluster to see whether early- vs late-diverging genes implicate different pathways
Significant pathways (BH-adjusted q<0.05) are reported with gene overlap counts; if no pathway reaches significance, that null result is stated rather than reporting nominal p-values as findings
If none of the pathway gene-set files are found in the environment at run time, the step reports this explicitly and stops rather than fabricating enrichment results

plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in bulk RNA-seq time course
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2-condition x 4-timepoint (t0..t3) bulk RNA-seq time course with 3 replicates per cell (24 samples, 12000 genes, raw salmon counts in counts.csv, sample metadata with condition/time/time_hours in metadata.csv). The research question — which genes change over time in a treatment-specific way, beyond the trend shared by both conditions — is precisely a condition:time interaction test in a factorial time-course design. We build a DESeqDataSet from the raw counts and metadata, QC the samples (library size, PCA, sample-distance clustering) to confirm the 2x4x3 structure holds and flag any outlier replicate before modeling. We then fit DESeq2's likelihood-ratio test comparing a full model (~condition + time + condition:time) against a reduced model (~condition + time): genes significant in this LRT show curvature over time that differs between conditions, i.e. a treatment-specific temporal effect on top of whatever both conditions do in common. For interaction-significant genes we extract per-timepoint, per-condition trajectories from variance-stabilized expression and cluster them to describe qualitatively how the divergence unfolds (early vs late onset, transient vs sustained, up- vs down-diverging) rather than reporting only a gene list. Finally we run pathway over-representation on the interaction gene set against WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark/GO-BP gene sets (both staged for Homo sapiens, matching the taxon 9606 dataset) to characterize which biological processes carry the treatment-specific temporal signature.
